agent.name: Emerging Technology Creation Agent
agent.specialty: Technology creation, predecessor capabilities, enabling conditions and contextual implications

analytical_question: How did instruction-tuned LLMs arise, and what does that history imply for the consulting research assistant?
general_et_finding: LLMs emerged from efforts to make language processing more flexible and easier to direct. Attention-based architectures, large-scale text pretraining and human-feedback tuning combined to support reusable language capabilities. The selected milestones show cumulative development rather than a technology appearing fully formed.
application_finding: Inference: document synthesis is a plausible application of reusable language capabilities, but generated summaries still require source checking.
organization_specific_finding: Inference: the small consulting firm can explore an existing model rather than train one; its public-document scope and analyst review limit the consequences of mistakes.

evidence.claim: The Transformer combined attention-based sequence modeling with a more parallelizable architecture, demonstrated on translation tasks.
evidence.source_or_reference: Vaswani et al. (2017), Attention Is All You Need. https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762
evidence.date_or_recency: Published 2017; abstract and submission history checked 2026-10-06 UTC
evidence.notes: Historical architecture evidence; not proof of performance in either hypothetical organization.

evidence.claim: GPT-3 demonstrated task adaptation from text examples without task-specific parameter updates, with uneven results across tasks.
evidence.source_or_reference: Brown et al. (2020), Language Models are Few-Shot Learners. https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165
evidence.date_or_recency: Published 2020; abstract and submission history checked 2026-10-06 UTC
evidence.notes: Supports a historical scaling and pretraining milestone; not a current model benchmark.

evidence.claim: InstructGPT combined supervised demonstrations and human-preference reinforcement learning; instruction-following improved but mistakes remained.
evidence.source_or_reference: Ouyang et al. (2022), Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback. https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155
evidence.date_or_recency: Published 2022; abstract and submission history checked 2026-10-06 UTC
evidence.notes: Supports the distinction between instruction-following and guaranteed correctness.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: The historical studies do not test this firm or its documents.
The three milestones are not a complete account of language-model history.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence in the selected historical milestones; uncertain performance and benefits in this organization.
value_opportunity_implication: Potential reduction in drafting effort; no measured savings are available.
risk_governance_implication: Retain analyst review because plausible text is not necessarily supported by source material.
recommendation_management_implication: Explore a bounded pilot of internal summaries and review the results before wider adoption.
change_monitoring_triggers: Reassess as technology improves or organizational needs change.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Representative documents and a specified model are needed to assess actual quality.
